sections.title: Bringing Unit 17 together
sections.content: This lesson pulls together Unit 17: saying what hurts with fáj and a possessive suffix on the body part, describing symptoms with a van-pattern (lázam van), asking Mi a baj? or Hol fáj?, saying how long with -ja/-je, and understanding the doctor and pharmacist.

sections.title: Health and the body, recapped
rows: fever, to cough, to feel dizzy
for two days, for a week

items.spanish: Két napja fáj a torkom, és köhögök.
items.english: My throat has hurt for two days, and I'm coughing.

items.spanish: Mi a panasza? – Lázam van, és fáj a fejem.
items.english: What's your complaint? – I have a fever, and my head hurts.

items.spanish: Az orvos felírt egy gyógyszert a láz ellen.
items.english: The doctor prescribed a medicine against the fever.

sections.content: Mi a baj? is the casual way to ask what's wrong among friends; Mi a panasza? is what a doctor asks a patient formally. Both are answered the same way: name the body part or symptom, with fáj or van.
